/LILIAN

Baltic Exchange Market Report 05 October 2026
Baltic Dry Index: 3070 (-78)
Baltic Capesize Index: 4833 (-209)
Baltic Panamax Index: 2364 (-8)
Baltic Supramax Index: 1790 (1)
Baltic Handysize Index: 1004 (-3)
CAPESIZE
The Capesize market began the week with a reasonable flow of West Australia cargoes from both miners and operators in the Pacific. Despite public holidays in Korea and China, activity persisted with fixtures reported in the high $13s and low $14s across a range of loading windows. The C5 index eased by $0.40 to $14.025. Meanwhile, the Brazil/West Africa market continued to soften after fixtures were reported around $37.00 late last week, resulting in the C3 index falling a further $0.80 to $36.850. After both routes lost around $1,700, round voyage earnings on the China-Brazil/West Africa route remained above those of the transpacific run. Further market discussion emerged from the Atlantic, including a handful of Newcastlemax fixtures from Friday, though these were not necessarily concluded at firmer levels. The BCI 182 5TC posted a loss of $1,898 to $43,833 today.

Atlantic
Vale took a vessel for 160,000/10 PDM to Ijmuiden 1/10 November at $19.50. Vitol was rumoured to have taken the Cape Magnolia (181,461 2011) for 185,000/10 Nouadhibou to Qingdao in end October at a rate in the high $30s. A Newcastlemax was linked to Anglo’s 190,000/10 Saldanha Bay to Qingdao 24/30 October at a rate in the low $27s.

Asia
There was talk of BHP taking a vessel for 160,000/10 Port Hedland to Qingdao 22/24 October in the very low $14s. Rio Tinto fixed a few vessels for 170,000/10 Dampier to Qingdao from 17 Oct onwards at $13.95.
PANAMAX
Market sources today reported slower fixing activity across both basins, with the P5TC declining by $76 to $21,273. Trans-Atlantic and fronthaul business is said to be characterised by a wide bid-offer spread, with both Owners and Charterers showing less willingness to close the gap as participants take stock of their positions in an effort to gain a clearer sense of market direction. Some brokers have suggested that tonnage is beginning to build off the North Continent, a development which could weigh on rates should demand fail to improve. Others, however, argue that the headline tonnage count is misleading, noting that the number of vessels genuinely available and not already pencilled in for cargoes presents a more balanced picture. Activity in the Pacific is similarly subdued today due to the various national holidays across the region. Despite the quieter trading environment, market fundamentals are said to remain fairly evenly balanced. Indonesian demand continues to be relatively limited, although Australian demand is still reported to be providing a steady source of enquiry and is helping to support a generally positive sentiment among Owners.
SUPRAMAX
The usual slow start to a new week, with collection mode evident the 11 TC average today was $22,620, up just $1 from Fridays close. There was a rumour of a well described 64,000-dwt coming from Chile being on subjects basis delivery Recalada for a trip Singapore-Japan range at $20,000 plus $1,000,000 ballast bonus, reinforcing the firm tone in the South Atlantic. There was little reported elsewhere in the Atlantic, although the US Gulf slide a little lower in the index and the Mediterranean remains subdued. In Asia, NoPac and backhaul demand continues to support the market, which in turn has fuelled period activity. The Belfast (63,685 2021) prompt in the Philippines fixed a trip via Indonesia to Thailand at $25,000 and the Uniwell (52,454 2006) fixed delivery Salalah for a trip EC India at $18,000, but in both cases the Charterer was not revealed. The BBG Guilin (61,189 2021) Zhoushan 5-10 October fixed 5 to 7 months in the mid $23,000’s, again to an unnamed interest.
HANDYSIZE
The week opened quietly across both the Atlantic and Pacific markets, with participants largely in a collecting mood. No fresh activity emerged from the US Gulf or South Atlantic, where fundamentals remained relatively soft. A 29,000-dwt vessel was heard fixed for a trip from Walvis Bay to China with concentrates at $14,000, although further details were not confirmed. The Continent and Mediterranean maintained a flat tone, with fragile but broadly balanced fundamentals. The Pacific market also began the week on a slightly softer note, with little change in conditions and no clear direction emerging. The UM Mogami (40,631 2026) open Ningde was fixed for a backhaul trip to the Continent with deck and project cargo in the mid-$21,000s. The Kangting (37,440 2020) open Busan prompt was fixed by Pangaea for two to three laden legs, with the first leg carrying cement to the US West Coast, at $19,000, although further details were not disclosed. Reflecting these regional differences, the BHSI slipped by 3 points to 1,004, while the 7TC average fell by $50 to close at $18,067.

Market Fundamentals
Indian September Coal Output and Dispatches Rise
Indian state-owned miner, Coal India Ltd (CIL), recorded a 9% year-on-year rise in production to 53.5 Mt in September, McCloskey reports. Meanwhile, dispatches jumped 13% year-on-year to 61.2 Mt. The miner cited favourable post-monsoon weather compared to last year as the reason for the improvement, with coal supplies to the power sector up 11% on the year to 48.9 Mt.
Sent from Front

Trading Commentary
Cape
Cape was mixed through the session, with a stronger afternoon recovery after a softer morning. Oct started around 38,500 before slipping to 38,000, then recovered to 38,750 before finishing around 38,500. Nov traded around 39,500 through much of the morning before firming strongly to 40,500–40,600 in the afternoon closing at 40,250. Dec traded mainly 39,500–40,000. Q4 26 was active around 39,100–39,350 early before recovering to 39,750 late. Q1 27 traded mostly 28,750–29,300, while Q2 27 printed 34,650–35,000. Cal 27 moved from around 32,100 to 32,500 late, while Cal 28 traded 27,500–27,700.

PMX
PMX was steady early before firming through the afternoon. Oct traded around 21,150–21,250 early before moving up to 21,400–21,450 later. Nov spent much of the morning around 21,150 before firming to 21,300–21,400. Dec was steady around 21,150–21,250. Q4 26 traded mainly 21,200–21,350, finishing toward the highs. Q1 27 ranged between 17,250–17,400, while Q2 27 recovered from 18,250 to 18,450. Q3 27 moved from 17,350 to 17,500. Further out, Cal 27 firmed from 17,300 to 17,550, while Cal 28 printed 15,300.
